newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa funds struggled to beat inflation in 1996.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa funds struggled to beat inflation in 1996.

text.p: South African fund managers struggled to beat inflation in 1996 with the average return achieved by investment houses and insurers 11.2 percent, according to a survey published on Thursday.
That compares with year-on-year consumer inflation of 9.4 percent in December and following a disappointing finish to the year in South African markets, First Bowring Insurance Brokers said.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange the all-share index dropped by 3.2 percent in the fourth quarter to finish the year up 6.9 percent.
The Board of Executors (BOE) and Investec have emerged as the country's leading fund performers, the broker said.

Among insurers, where First Bowring surveyed 19 funds and 12 managers, BOE Investors Fund came top for returns over the last three years with 18.5 percent. Investec Managed Fund had the best quarterly return in the last quarter of 1996 with 4.6 percent.

Among investment houses, where 17 funds were surveyed from 12 asset management companies, the top performers over the last three years were BOE, Fleming Martin, Coronation, Investec and ABSA, in that order. All had returns above 16 percent a year.
For last year, the best investment house performance came from AFC with 16.2 percent, the closest rival being Investec with 13.1 percent.
Commenting on the results, BOE managing director John Winship said the good performance was attributable more to equity selection than aggressive market weightings.
